brief_item.title: PTStore：借鉴CDN把可复用KV前缀张量分布复制到多节点
brief_item.direction_name: KVCache感知的网络与带宽调度
brief_item.core_conclusion: 现有推理运行时KV缓存多困于单机，致跨节点复用需重算，PTStore用CDN思路把热前缀张量分布复制到多节点多卡以降低TTFT。
brief_item.mechanism: 借鉴CDN客户端缓存把可复用KV前缀张量增量存储并复制到各节点，用RDMA并行服务最长公共前缀查询。
brief_item.result: 长文问答上效率比不聚合内存的基线高5到6倍，8k token的TTFT约为vLLM前缀缓存的两倍速。
brief_item.boundary: 仅报告TTFT与端到端时间，未给TPOT或P95及生产硬件规模。
brief_item.project_relevance: 为分布式KV聚合改变存储网络边界提供参照，可评估热前缀复制对跨节点复用的收益。

facts.title: PTStore (Prefix Tensor Store): Distributed Prefix Caching and Replication for High Throughput Inference Serving
facts.event_hint: PTStore: a distributed prefix caching and replication system that stores reusable KV-cache prefix tensors across nodes/GPUs to accelerate LLM inference, from JHU and Argonne.
facts.problem: Existing inference runtimes (vLLM, DeepSpeed-MII, LMCache, Mooncake, SGLang) cache KV results mostly in local GPU/host memory; they lack support for aggregating distributed memory tiers, so cross-node prefix reuse requires regenerating the KV cache, causing load imbalance when popular tensors concentrate on a few servers and capping total KV-cache capacity.
facts.mechanism: Inspired by CDN client-caching, PTStore distributes and replicates popular tensors that form reusable KV-cache prefixes across distributed nodes and GPUs. It uses incremental tensor storage to minimize redundancy, consolidated metadata for rapid longest-common-prefix (LCP) queries, and a replication strategy optimizing local access to hot prefixes. Clients issue LCP queries (broadcast+reduce) and read/write tensor subsets via optimized RDMA built on the Mochi composable stack (Thallium C++ wrapper over Mercury and Argobots), progressing multiple servers in parallel. It integrates with existing LLM runtimes (e.g., vLLM).

evidence.claim: PTStore executes inferences on long-passage Q&A datasets 5-6 times more efficiently than current baselines that do not aggregate memory across nodes/GPUs and therefore regenerate the KV cache.
evidence.baseline: baselines that do not aggregate memory across nodes/GPUs (require KV cache regeneration)
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: In TTFT scalability tests (1k-8k tokens, vLLM, SQUAD), PTStore outperforms vLLM's prefix caching starting at 2k tokens and is almost 2x faster at 8k tokens.
evidence.condition: vLLM runtime, SQUAD dataset, 8k token sequences, TTFT metric
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12 - Fig.4a

evidence.claim: PTStore is more than 2x faster than EvoStore for 1k-token sequences and about 20% faster for 8k tokens, with the advantage attributed to prefix replication (Fig.4b I/O vs compute breakdown).
evidence.condition: TTFT, SQUAD dataset, 1k and 8k token sequences
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12

evidence.claim: Experimental evaluations show PTStore significantly reduces Time to First Token (TTFT) versus state of the art by up to an order of magnitude and remains scalable across variable sequence lengths.
evidence.value: up to an order of magnitude
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12 - 7 Conclusions

evidence.claim: Workloads use WikiQA (3,000 questions, page lengths 2,000-40,000 tokens) for scaling experiments and SQUAD (100,000 questions) for reading-comprehension extractive tasks; both are long-prompt/short-answer workloads that stress the prefill stage.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 9 - Workloads

facts.evaluation_context: Research prototype (JHU + Argonne) evaluated on extractive long-context Q&A (WikiQA, SQUAD). Communication uses optimized bulk RDMA via Mochi/Thallium. Reported metrics focus on TTFT and end-to-end runtime; sequence lengths tested 1k-8k tokens. No TPOT, token throughput, network utilization, or end-to-end P95 latency numbers are visible in the Evidence Pack; no production hardware spec or deployment scale (node/GPU counts) is exposed.
facts.limitations: TTFT and end-to-end runtime are the main reported metrics; decode-phase (TPOT), token throughput, and P95 latency are not reported in the visible evidence. Hardware platform, exact node/GPU counts, and RDMA fabric specs are not exposed. Results are specific to extractive long-context Q&A workloads (long prompt, short answer) which favor prefill optimization; performance on short prompts or decode-heavy chat workloads is not characterized. For small query lengths vLLM's baseline prefix caching is superior, per the authors.
facts.project_relevance: PTStore is a distributed prefix-cache storage layer using RDMA for cross-node KV-cache access, directly relevant to KVCache-aware network/bandwidth scheduling and the TPN question of whether network-side mechanisms reduce cross-node KVCache transfer and improve TTFT. It offers a concrete reference point for how distributed KV-cache aggregation changes the storage/network boundary, though it is a research prototype, not an Alibaba TPN product.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.22648v1 (25 Jun 2026), FETCHED primary source.
Headline 5-6x efficiency gain is an abstract claim whose detailed baseline and workload condition are restated but the exact measurement table is in the unread suffix.
Comparison baselines are explicitly named: vLLM (prefix caching), EvoStore; related systems discussed include LMCache, Mooncake, SGLang (RadixAttention), Splitwise, DistServe.

brief_item.title: SK hynix与SanDisk发布首个开放高带宽闪存HBF标准
brief_item.core_conclusion: AI推理同时受带宽与容量挤压，SK hynix与SanDisk经OCP发布首个开放高带宽闪存HBF标准，填补HBM与SSD之间的新层。
brief_item.mechanism: 用堆叠NAND die提供类HBM高速传输并扩容，经UCIe可接GPU或CPU。
brief_item.result: 规范容量至512GB分8层与16层堆叠，带宽分三档约从0.4到3.0TB每秒。
brief_item.boundary: 仅为公告阶段规范未给耐久时延功耗或量产时间等实测。
brief_item.project_relevance: UCIe开放标准化利处理器无关部署，但项目须区分公告规范与量产能力再纳入存储分层。

facts.title: SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications with SanDisk at FMS 2026
facts.event_hint: SK hynix and Sandisk published first open High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) standard specification via OCP at FMS 2026.
facts.problem: AI inference drives surging data volumes; existing memory hierarchy faces simultaneous bandwidth and capacity scalability bottlenecks that neither HBM nor SSDs alone resolve.
facts.mechanism: HBF is a new memory layer positioned between HBM and SSDs: it uses stacked NAND dies to deliver HBM-like high-speed transfer while significantly expanding capacity. The stack comes in 8-high and 16-high NAND die configurations; the host interconnect adopts the UCIe industry standard so HBF can attach to different processor types (GPUs, CPUs). The spec also defines connection interfaces/electrical characteristics, reliability and die-stack packaging guidelines, and software I/O guidelines.

evidence.claim: First HBF standard specification unveiled by SK hynix in collaboration with Sandisk via the Open Compute Project (OCP), positioned as an open industry standard.
evidence.baseline: proprietary technology / no prior open HBF spec
evidence.condition: announced August 4, 2026 at FMS 2026, Santa Clara
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: SK hynix Unveils First HBF Standard Specifications with Sandisk ... – Seoul, August 4, 2026

evidence.claim: HBF capacity specifications cover up to 512GB, based on two stack configurations: 8-high and 16-high NAND dies.
evidence.source_locator: Capacity specifications cover up to 512GB based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies)

evidence.claim: HBF bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s.
evidence.source_locator: Bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s

evidence.claim: HBF adopts UCIe as the interconnect linking HBF to processors, enabling flexible integration across GPU and CPU processor types.
evidence.source_locator: HBF technology adopts UCIe, an industry standard connection interface, laying the groundwork to flexibly integrate HBF technology across different processor types, including GPUs and CPUs

evidence.claim: The HBF consortium launched in February 2026, about six months before this spec, following the initial standardization partnership with Sandisk in August 2025; Google and Tenstorrent currently participate.
evidence.source_locator: This milestone comes about six months after launching the consortium in February this year, following the initial standardization partnership with Sandisk in August 2025 ... With Google and Tenstorrent currently participating in the HBF consortium

facts.evaluation_context: Announcement-stage standard specification, not a measured product benchmark. No workload, hardware platform, latency, endurance (P/E), write-amplification, or power measurement is exposed in the visible evidence. Capacity (up to 512GB) and bandwidth (~0.4-3.0TB/s across Grade1-3) are specified ranges, not validated system results.
facts.limitations: Evidence is a vendor newsroom announcement of a specification, not independent characterization. No P/E endurance, access latency, write amplification, power draw, cost/bit, or volume-production timeline is visible. Headline summary claims of ~2.5x power-efficiency gain and ~540x capacity vs HBM are not supported by the visible Evidence Pack text and were not recorded as facts. Maturity (sampling vs mass production) is unspecified.
facts.project_relevance: HBF targets the AI inference bandwidth/capacity gap that influences storage-hierarchy and memory-attachment decisions. UCIe-based open standardization matters for processor-agnostic deployment, but the project card requires distinguishing announced specs from sampled or mass-production capability; here only an open specification and consortium status are confirmed.
source_notes: Source is an SK hynix newsroom announcement (vendor primary) loaded as LOCAL_SOURCE; numbers are specification targets, not measured benchmarks.
Discovery summary mentions ~2.5x power-efficiency improvement and ~540x capacity vs HBM, but these statements are absent from the visible Evidence Pack and were treated as unverified claims.

brief_item.title: ThAME：3D FeFET加层次NoC在仿真上同时解MoE推理的两道墙
brief_item.direction_name: AI计算芯片与加速器架构
brief_item.core_conclusion: MoE推理受专家权重带宽与非确定token路由双重夹击，ThAME用3D FeFET加DRAM多芯粒与层次NoC，在仿真上同时解这两道墙。
brief_item.mechanism: 把专家权重存于片上3D FeFET-NAND并用AMOSA设计的层次NoC缓解非确定路由流量。
brief_item.result: 仿真上相对Stratum等基线最高加速15.7倍能效提升9.8倍达147.5 Tokens每秒每瓦。
brief_item.boundary: 全部为周期级仿真无流片，未给端到端服务P95。
brief_item.project_relevance: 为FeFET近存计算进入AI内存层级提供架构投影，须等流片或预硅验证再判断。

facts.title: ThAME: 3D Memory-Enabled Heterogeneous Accelerator for LLM Mixture of Experts
facts.event_hint: ThAME: a proposed 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet accelerator combining FeFET-NAND and DRAM memory chiplets with a co-designed hierarchical NoC for MoE LLM inference (architecture study, not silicon).
facts.problem: MoE inference on conventional hardware is bottlenecked by three issues: massive memory bandwidth needed to fetch non-contiguous expert weights, non-deterministic scatter-gather traffic from input-dependent token routing, and tail-latency dependency from synchronous expert output aggregation. Expert weights dominate model size (>90%) and existing memory hierarchies cannot balance density, leakage and access latency.
facts.mechanism: ThAME is a 3D heterogeneous multi-chiplet architecture using FeFET (ferroelectric FET) non-volatile and DRAM volatile memory chiplets with a co-designed compute mapping that aligns attention and expert routing profiles. It stores expert weights on-chip in 3D FeFET-NAND to break the memory wall, and adds a specialized hierarchical Network-on-Chip (designed via Archived Multi-Objective Simulated Annealing, AMOSA) inside the FeFET-NAND die to mitigate non-deterministic token-routing traffic. Evaluated config: two FeFET and two DRAM memory chiplets plus a systolic-array (TPU v6e) host chiplet on a silicon interposer, point-to-point connected.

evidence.claim: ThAME outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts by up to 15.7x speedup and improves energy efficiency by up to 9.8x.
evidence.value: up to 15.7x speedup; up to 9.8x energy efficiency
evidence.condition: abstract headline; detailed baseline/workload in results
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: ThAME delivers 147.5 Tokens/s/W, a 5.6x, 20.9x and 31.7x improvement over Stratum, TPU v6e and NVIDIA A100 baselines respectively; normalized by silicon area it reaches 184.3 Tokens/s/kW/mm^2.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13

evidence.claim: At batch size B=64 (Deepseek model, MMLU), ThAME delivers up to 5.92x and 12.77x higher throughput than Stratum and H3D-T respectively; the gap widens with batch size due to Stratum/H3D-T network contention.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Scalability

evidence.claim: Co-design decomposition: swapping ThAME's hierarchical NoC for a Mesh topology degrades latency up to 1.44x and energy efficiency up to 2.1x; substituting FeFET-NAND with DRAM-PNM adds up to 1.8x energy overhead; synergistic co-design yields 4.7x/7.0x latency and 5.4x/8.7x energy efficiency gains over Stratum for Qwen1.5 and Deepseek respectively.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 11

evidence.claim: Evaluation uses cycle-accurate simulators: SCALE-Sim for systolic array latency (median error <3% vs production TPU), NeuroSim for FeFET-NAND 3D arrays (chip-level error <1% after calibration), BookSim2 for intra-chiplet NoC, HotSpot for thermal; 16-bit fixed-point precision; MoE models Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B and dense Llama3-8B.
evidence.condition: 45C ambient, 50W base die budget, 4096 PEs/core, 32-core system, 121mm^2 base die
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 8 - Experimental Setup

facts.evaluation_context: Architecture study evaluated entirely via cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim, NeuroSim, BookSim2, HotSpot), not taped-out silicon. 16-bit fixed-point precision. Config: 2 FeFET + 2 DRAM chiplets + TPU v6e host on silicon interposer, 32-core/4096-PE system, 121mm^2 base die, 50W base-die thermal budget at 45C ambient. Baselines: Stratum (DRAM-PNM), H3D-T (3D FeFET/SRAM/TPU), TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100. MoE workloads: Deepseek-16B, Olmoe-1B, Qwen1.5-2.7B, Qwen3-30B; dense Llama3-8B.
facts.limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-accurate modeling, calibrated but not silicon measurements); no real chip, no deployment. HBF reference (SK Hynix H^3 up to 2.69x throughput-per-watt) is cited as related context, not a ThAME measurement. The evaluated chiplet count/config is one specific point; authors note it does not affect generalizability but other configs are not shown. Decode-phase token latency and end-to-end serving P95 are not reported; metrics focus on speedup, energy efficiency, Tokens/s/W and throughput scaling. FeFET device variability/endurance is acknowledged as a memory-technology trade-off but not quantified in results.
facts.project_relevance: ThAME directly addresses the MoE memory-wall and intra-chiplet routing problem relevant to AI accelerator architecture and memory-IO codesign: it couples high-density 3D FeFET-NAND storage with a specialized NoC. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture proposal (not pre-silicon validation or production), so its system claims are architectural projections rather than measured silicon. The HBF/FeFET angle also touches the storage-media question of whether NAND-based near-memory compute can enter the AI memory hierarchy.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17074v2 (19 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source.
All performance numbers come from cycle-accurate simulation (SCALE-Sim/NeuroSim/BookSim2/HotSpot), not silicon.
Baselines are explicitly named: Stratum, H3D-T, TPU v6e, NVIDIA A100.

brief_item.title: D-NOVA：双界相似度感知把向量检索直接做进3D NAND阵列
brief_item.core_conclusion: RAG向量检索是主时延瓶颈，既有存内加速仍把重排留给处理器，D-NOVA用双界相似度感知把IVF检索直接做进3D NAND阵列，避免数据搬移。
brief_item.mechanism: 用双界紧相似度感知把向量检索化为对NAND阈值电平的查询相关门限搜索，仅紧凑分数离开阵列。
brief_item.result: 仿真上比CPU基线快41.7倍能效71倍，相对REIS时延降至约四分之一。
brief_item.boundary: 仿真基于QLC NAND无流片，未给端到端RAG时延或耐久影响。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示NAND阵列可承担AI检索角色，为存内计算改变存储层级边界提供仿真依据。

facts.title: D-NOVA: In-Storage Retrieval Accelerator via Dual-Bound 3D NAND-Optimized Similarity Search with Vector Adaptation
facts.event_hint: D-NOVA: an in-storage vector retrieval accelerator for RAG that embeds IVF-based similarity search directly into 3D NAND arrays using Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS) and a contrastive vector adapter (MICRO 2026).
facts.problem: Dense vector retrieval in RAG is the primary latency/energy bottleneck. Existing in-storage/near-storage accelerators (SmartSSD, RAGX, REIS) still rely on host/embedded processors for final re-ranking; in REIS this INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by multi-level cell read latency and data movement to the embedded processor, creating a new memory wall.
facts.mechanism: D-NOVA executes an IVF-based hierarchical retrieval pipeline entirely inside the NAND array. It introduces Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS), a distance metric that reformulates vector retrieval as a query-dependent threshold search over ordered V_TH levels using complement sensing and compact scoring within the NAND string. A lightweight contrastive adapter maps embedding vectors into a DTS-friendly domain to recover near-software recall. Only compact scores/metadata leave the array; full embeddings never move off-array. D-NOVA reuses existing page-buffer structures in binary pass/fail mode, preserving standard QLC read/program compatibility and achieving SLC-like read latency at QLC density.

evidence.claim: D-NOVA is up to 41.7x faster and 71x more energy-efficient than a CPU baseline, and achieves 12.13x higher throughput while being up to 1.26x more energy-efficient than state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators.
evidence.baseline: CPU baseline; state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators
evidence.condition: abstract headline; per-workload breakdown in results
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: In prior in-storage accelerators, the off-array INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by MLC read latency and data movement to the embedded processor.
evidence.condition: REIS-style in-storage accelerators with controller-side re-ranking
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - REIS analysis

evidence.claim: D-NOVA and D-NOVA-F sustain roughly 481-679x of the CPU QPS and about 42.7-67.9x of the NSP baseline throughput; relative to REIS, D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F improve throughput by ~4.3-6.1x and D-NOVA-XF reaches ~8.6-12.1x higher QPS.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12 - Throughput Improvement

evidence.claim: Compared to REIS, D-NOVA reduces latency by 3.01-3.79x, D-NOVA-F by 3.80-4.99x, and D-NOVA-XF by 5.98-7.53x, with additional energy savings of 6-27% by avoiding off-array final re-ranking.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12

evidence.claim: Simulated on QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string, 8.5V window, PTM-MG 14nm) using Spectre circuit simulation and Monte Carlo V_TH variation modeling; config: PCIe 4.0x4 host, 8 flash channels (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/ch, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth; shared accumulator adds 0.023 mm^2/plane (<1.5% of 1.476 mm^2 plane area) synthesized at ASAP7 7nm.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 9 - Tables 1 & 2; PDF Page 12 - 6.7 Overhead

facts.evaluation_context: Simulated in-storage NVMe SSD subsystem (not silicon). QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string), 8 flash channels at 2.0 GB/s/channel (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/channel, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth, PCIe 4.0x4 host interface. Circuit-level validation via Spectre 19.1 (PTM-MG 14nm) with Monte Carlo V_TH mismatch and QLC drift modeling; accumulator synthesized with ASAP7 7nm at 1 GHz. Workloads: BEIR/NQ, HotpotQA, synthetic dataset (16GB-120GB); embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and all-mpnet-base-v2. Baselines: CPU-IVF (FAISS IVF-Flat on dual-socket 128-core server, 1.5TB DDR4), NSP baseline, REIS.
facts.limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD model plus Spectre/Monte Carlo circuit simulation), not measurements from fabricated silicon. Read latency/energy parameters are rescaled from prior measured NAND data (294.9 nJ/page read, 30us SLC / 140us QLC). Absolute end-to-end RAG serving latency (including LLM generation) is not reported; metrics focus on retrieval stage. Endurance/write-amplification impact of DTS sensing on QLC cells is not quantified in the visible evidence. DTS sensing resolution degrades at larger simultaneous-cell count m, a tradeoff tuned per config.
facts.project_relevance: D-NOVA is a NAND-centric in-storage compute design that pushes vector search into the flash array, directly relevant to whether 3D NAND can take on AI-serving storage-hierarchy roles (RAG retrieval) beyond bulk storage. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture study showing how in-array sensing can convert NAND density into retrieval throughput/energy gains; it is not a product or deployed system. The QLC-density-at-SLC-latency claim touches the storage-media density/bandwidth/latency questions.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17538v1 (20 Jul 2026), to appear MICRO 2026; FETCHED primary source; authors from UC San Diego.
All performance numbers are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD simulator + Spectre/Monte Carlo), not silicon measurements.
Baselines explicitly named: CPU-IVF (FAISS on 128-core server), NSP near-storage processor, REIS in-storage; D-NOVA variants D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F/D-NOVA-XF differ by (m1,m2,m3) multi-cell sensing config.

facts.title: Kioxia and SanDisk 10th-Gen 332-Layer QLC NAND Achieves Industry's Highest Bit Density
facts.event_hint: Kioxia + SanDisk unveil 10th-generation 332-layer QLC 3D NAND at FMS 2026 (Aug 4, 2026): >37 Gb/mm^2 bit density (industry-leading claim), 4.8 Gb/s interface, CBA architecture.
facts.problem: AI training, inference and hyperscale datacenter workloads are driving rapid data-volume growth, putting pressure on storage to deliver higher capacity, higher performance and improved energy efficiency simultaneously. The release positions prior QLC 3D NAND generations as unable to meet this combined density+bandwidth+power envelope for next-generation AI/cloud infrastructure.
facts.mechanism: 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory with a 332-layer architecture and optimized floorplan. Built on CMOS directly Bonded to Array (CBA) technology, which fabricates CMOS logic and the memory array on separate wafers in their optimized conditions and then bonds them with high-precision wafer-to-wafer alignment, enhancing density scaling, performance and manufacturing efficiency. The 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface is enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 plus the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol. Power-Isolated Low-Tapped Termination (PI-LTT) improves I/O data-out transfer power efficiency. The combination is claimed to deliver simultaneous gains in density, bandwidth and energy efficiency.

evidence.claim: The 332-layer architecture and optimized floorplan deliver up to a 60% increase in bit density, achieving >37 Gb/mm^2 compared to the 8th-generation, claimed as the industry benchmark for QLC NAND bit density.
evidence.condition: 10th-generation QLC 3D flash, 332-layer; Kioxia/SanDisk survey as of August 3, 2026
evidence.source_locator: Press release: Key 10th-generation QLC 3D flash memory technology highlights (bulleted list)

evidence.claim: It is the industry's first QLC 3D flash memory technology to reach a 4.8 Gb/s NAND interface, enabled by Toggle DDR6.0 and the Separate Command Address (SCA) protocol.
evidence.baseline: prior QLC 3D NAND interfaces (none had reached 4.8 Gb/s)

facts.evaluation_context: Source type: joint vendor press release from Kioxia Corporation and Sandisk Corporation, unveiled at the Future of Memory and Storage (FMS) 2026 conference, Santa Clara, CA, August 4, 2026. Product class: 10th-generation QLC (Quad-Level-Cell) 3D NAND flash, 332 layers, CBA architecture, Toggle DDR6.0 + SCA interface at 4.8 Gb/s, PI-LTT termination. Target applications stated: AI storage architectures, cloud platforms, data-intensive innovation, agent-based and physical AI. 'Industry's highest'/'industry benchmark'/'industry's first' claims are based on Kioxia and SanDisk survey as of August 3, 2026.
facts.limitations: This is a product announcement press release, not a measured characterization paper. No quantitative P/E endurance, write amplification, random/sequential read-write throughput (IOPS/MB/s), access latency, $/bit, die size, or power draw figures are disclosed. The 4.8 Gb/s interface value is explicitly vendor-test-environment-specific and 'may vary depending on use conditions'. The 'up to 60%' density gain and 'improved read/write bandwidth' are directional and not given as absolute numbers. Mass-production / sampling / commercialization timing is not specified in the release (Kioxia CTO only says they 'will accelerate development toward commercialization'), so this is an announcement, not a shipping product. The 'industry's highest/first' benchmarks are self-surveyed as of Aug 3, 2026.
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to the storage-media card's question of whether NAND density/bandwidth/power evolution is crossing into system-usable territory for AI storage tiers: 332-layer QLC at >37 Gb/mm^2 with a 4.8 Gb/s interface is a concrete generational step that, combined with PI-LTT power-efficiency improvement, targets the AI/cloud capacity-per-watt envelope. However, the absence of endurance, latency and absolute throughput numbers means it cannot yet be judged whether this changes the storage hierarchy boundary (e.g., versus HBF or against persistent-memory tiers). It is best treated as a credible announcement signal pending characterization and a commercialization timeline. Verification gap: obtain P/E endurance, write amplification, measured random/sequential throughput, latency and mass-production schedule before treating it as a deployable capability.

facts.title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
facts.event_hint: KAP (Knowledge Access Planning): a serving-time IR that compiles structured knowledge priors (e.g. GraphRAG) into a runtime access plan governing physical KV access, instantiated as GraphSpec on a vLLM backend.
facts.problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: knowledge-selection frontends (RAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG) produce structured priors, but prompt serialization collapses them into a flat token stream, forcing the serving backend to densely consume the full KV state during decoding. Richer contexts enlarge the KV footprint and decode-time memory traffic, increasing latency and degrading throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of the context.
facts.mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors into first-class physical execution artifacts via a universal IR - the runtime access plan - which compiles knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training. GraphSpec is a compiler-executor instantiation connecting a Graph-RAG frontend to a vLLM backend; it produces a selected-KV proposal view with full-context verification. A phase-boundary cost model characterizes the positive-speedup regime (margin h-s between acceptance rate h and retained-KV ratio s).

evidence.claim: Across 4K-128K long-context QA, GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K (10.8% at 64K, 40.1% at 4K) while maintaining answer quality comparable to full-context decoding.
evidence.condition: long-context QA, Graph-RAG frontend, vLLM backend
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 2; PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: GraphSpec improves decode throughput (TPS) over full-context baseline by 1.08x at 4K-16K, 1.09x at 32K, 1.13x at 64K, and 1.19x at 128K; speedup grows with context length as retained-KV ratio falls.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 2

evidence.claim: Answer quality is preserved: GraphSpec pass rate differs from full-context baseline by at most 0.3 percentage points at five of six lengths, and is 1.9 points higher at 64K; average similarity closely matched across 4K-128K (e.g., 0.741 vs 0.748 at 64K).
evidence.condition: LLM-as-judge pass rate at 0.5 threshold; independent human audit 95% agreement on 100 SPIQA samples
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 13 - Table 3; PDF Page 12 - Table 1

evidence.claim: Ablation (64K): Physical concat (same selected evidence materialized as shortened 0.95K prompt) pass rate falls to 73.9% vs 87.9% for GraphSpec; Random concat 49.7%, Local window 47.1%, confirming the runtime access plan - not prompt shortening - is the operative bridge.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 14 - Table 4

evidence.claim: Phase-boundary model consistency (RQ4): retained ratio s decreases from 0.401 (4K) to 0.055 (128K) while acceptance h stays high (0.953-0.962), so margin h-s grows from 0.557 to 0.897 and measured speedup rises from 1.08x to 1.19x without refitting the cost model.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 14 - Table 5

facts.evaluation_context: Long-context QA workloads (4K-128K tokens) with a Graph-RAG knowledge-selection frontend and vLLM serving backend. Quality metric: LLM-as-judge similarity in [0,1] with 0.5 pass threshold (4 dimensions: fact consistency 40%, information completeness 30%, logical structure 20%, expression quality 10%), independently audited against 3-annotator majority vote on 100 SPIQA samples (95% agreement). Efficiency metrics: decode throughput (TPS) and TTFT; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT (Graph-RAG evidence frozen before benchmarking). All serving-path measurements collected with diagnostic profiling disabled.
facts.limitations: Evaluation is limited to one KAP instantiation (GraphSpec with Graph-RAG frontend + vLLM backend); authors explicitly state empirical evidence does not exhaust the broader design space. Results are strongest for long-context QA where graph-derived priors ground in evidence spans; effectiveness for other frontends, plan compilers, access policies, or backends is unverified. TTFT is slightly worse for GraphSpec at several lengths (e.g., 1.56s vs 1.51s at 4K) because plan compilation and selected-KV materialization are included. No production deployment scale, GPU hardware spec, or cost data is reported in the visible evidence.
facts.project_relevance: KAP/GraphSpec is a serving-runtime/compiler optimization that reduces decode-time KV memory traffic by making structured knowledge priors executable - directly relevant to LLM serving efficiency and KV-cache management. It offers a concrete mechanism (runtime access plan IR) for decoupling physical KV consumption from prompt length. For the project card it is a research system evaluated on long-context QA, not a production deployment; its horizontal relevance is to inference serving rather than to the seven deep topics specifically.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.24260v1 (27 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from QiYuanLab.
Quality metric is LLM-as-judge (not human eval on all samples); independently audited on 100 SPIQA samples with 95% judge-human agreement.
Backend is vLLM; frontend is Graph-RAG; baselines are full-context vLLM, physical/random/local-window concat.

_provenance.source_title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems

facts.title: Deltoris: Enabling Real-time VLA Inference in Embodied AI via Bit-level Sparsity and Speculative Inference
facts.event_hint: Deltoris: an algorithm-hardware co-design framework accelerating diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) inference for embodied AI using temporal-aware bit-sparsity, speculative inference, and a 1D systolic bit-serial PE array accelerator.
facts.problem: Diffusion-based VLA models produce smooth motion and good generalization for robot control but are compute-intensive and must run at high control frequency (50-200 Hz), imposing strict latency/energy constraints on edge devices. Existing robotic platforms miss real-time targets: the PAD VLA model runs at only 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin SoC.
facts.mechanism: Deltoris exploits high temporal similarity in robotic control loops (over 98% of pixels between consecutive camera frames are often unchanged). (1) A temporal-aware bit-sparsity algorithm computes only the differences between consecutive inputs, representing differential inputs in binary and executing only active '1' bits (up to 92.9% operation reduction). (2) A speculative inference technique (inspired by LLM speculative decoding) lets a lightweight VLA model predict multiple future actions that a heavier VLA model validates, amortizing weight/intermediate data loading across validation steps to cut the extra off-chip traffic that naive bit-sparsity would add (1.8x traffic increase). (3) A dedicated accelerator with customized 1D systolic bit-serial PE arrays and an output-stationary dataflow eliminates PE workload imbalance seen in prior bit-serial accelerators.

evidence.claim: Deltoris achieves up to 34.2x speedup over mobile GPUs and up to 6.1x over prior accelerators, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
evidence.condition: abstract headline; detailed baseline breakdown in results
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract

evidence.claim: The PAD VLA model executes at only 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin SoC, far below the 50-200 Hz real-time requirement, motivating the work.
evidence.condition: PAD model on Nvidia Jetson Orin SoC
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - Motivation

evidence.claim: Over 98% of pixels between consecutive camera frames often remain unchanged due to the small inter-control interval; the temporal-aware bit-sparsity algorithm achieves up to 92.9% operation reduction.
evidence.value: >98% pixels unchanged; up to 92.9% op reduction
evidence.condition: consecutive frames in robotic control loop
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - Motivation

evidence.claim: A naive bit-sparsity implementation increases off-chip data traffic by 1.8x, shifting workloads from compute-bound to memory-bound; the proposed speculative inference technique amortizes data loading across validation steps to mitigate this.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - Framework

evidence.claim: Hardware comparison: Deltoris (128 rows of PE array x 64 PEs, 2.45 mm^2 at 16nm) is compared against GPU (mobile Ampere in Nvidia Orin), Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion and Ditto; a speculative window size of 3 is reported as the best speedup/accuracy tradeoff.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 10 - Table 2; PDF Page 12

facts.evaluation_context: Algorithm-hardware co-design evaluated against six hardware baselines (mobile Ampere GPU in Nvidia Jetson Orin SoC, Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion, Ditto) with area reported at 16nm; default accelerator config 128 PE arrays x 64 PEs (2.45 mm^2). Accuracy evaluated on UVA-P (PushT) and UVA-L (LIBERO) datasets. Sensitivity studies cover PE array size, on-chip buffer size and speculation threshold. No end-to-end robot-task success-rate-vs-latency on physical hardware is in the visible evidence.
facts.limitations: Visible evidence focuses on algorithmic mechanism, hardware design, and speedup/energy sensitivity; the detailed end-to-end speedup breakdown by baseline and the absolute Hz achieved on the target platform are in results sections not fully exposed. Real-robot deployment latency (vs simulation/emulation) and power consumption in watts are not shown in the visible evidence. Accuracy is described as 'comparable' (negligible loss on UVA-P/UVA-L); a rapid-motion scenario accuracy figure is referenced (Fig.24) but its numeric result is not in the exposed text.
facts.project_relevance: Deltoris targets the compute and memory-traffic bottlenecks of diffusion-based VLA inference at the edge, relevant to AI accelerator architecture and HW/SW codesign. The bit-level temporal sparsity plus speculative-inference traffic amortization is a concrete mechanism for converting temporal redundancy into throughput. For the project card it is an accelerator/co-design study; the visible evidence does not establish production deployment or wafer-scale integration.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2608.04428v1 (5 Aug 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from SJTU, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute, ICT CAS.
Headline 34.2x/6.1x speedups are abstract claims; per-baseline numeric breakdown is partly in unexposed result tables.
Baselines explicitly named: mobile Ampere GPU (Nvidia Orin), Pragmatic, BBS, Cambricon-D, Exion, Ditto.

facts.title: Hawk: Harnessing Hardware-Aware Knowledge for High-Performance NPU Kernel Generation
facts.event_hint: Hawk: a training-free framework that uses hardware-aware knowledge (run-time synthesis, 2D retrieval, effect-driven distillation) to let LLMs generate high-performance Ascend NPU (Ascend C) kernels, targeting the Ascend Da Vinci architecture.
facts.problem: Generating high-performance NPU kernels with LLMs fails because LLMs lack hardware-specific priors: state-of-the-art LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C (vs 100%/80% on CUDA), over 75% of failures stem from low-level hardware-specific misuses, and even correct NPU kernels run ~20x slower than GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.
facts.mechanism: Hawk is a training-free framework with three modules. (1) Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis uses a Triple-Part Executable Knowledge Representation (indexing triggers, semantic rationales, exact syntactic templates) to couple error context with executable semantics, captured dynamically at run time. (2) Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval uses a 2D-Retrieval paradigm projecting queries into a syntactic space (API signature compliance) and a hardware-aligned semantic space (memory/parallelization constraints). (3) Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation uses LLM-driven semantic arbitration with physical NPU compilation/execution feedback to prune erroneous and redundant knowledge entries. Targets the Ascend Da Vinci architecture (AI Cube, AI Vector, multi-tier memory with MTE engines, explicit instruction pipelining).

evidence.claim: Hawk elevates NPU kernel generation accuracy from 49.4% to 80.0% and achieves up to 2.2x execution speedup over state-of-the-art baselines on real-world Ascend NPU workloads.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract; PDF Page 11 - Conclusion

evidence.claim: SOTA LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C, vs 100.0% Comp@1 and up to 86.7% Pass@1 on CUDA (DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5, 15 activation kernels from MultiKernelBench, add-shot prompting).
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GLM-4.5; 15 activation kernels; MultiKernelBench
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 3 - Table I

evidence.claim: Of 126 classified Ascend C generation failures, 98 (77.8%) are syntax-level (including 53 runtime timeouts, 27 non-existent functions) and 26 (20.6%) are hardware-level (UB overflow); only 2 (1.6%) are numeric correctness mismatches.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 3 - Table II

evidence.claim: Even functionally correct Ascend C kernels execute nearly 20x slower than their GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Introduction

evidence.claim: Sample timing on RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2 shows Ascend C kernels far slower than CUDA (e.g., diagonal op: CUDA 0.2ms vs Ascend 37.4ms, 295.6x normalized slowdown; ~22x slower vs PyTorch NPU baseline).
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 5 - Table IV

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on real-world Ascend NPU workloads (Ascend C kernels). LLMs tested: DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5 (plus supplementary DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Hardware platforms: RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2. Benchmark: MultiKernelBench, 15 activation kernels (L1/L2 coverage). Knowledge base covers 431 kernels across 8 development-paradigm dimensions. Baselines include fine-tuning (AscendKernelGen, EvoKernel) and IR-assisted frameworks (AKG, AscendCraft, STARK, CudaForge, AVO).
facts.limitations: Test suite covers L1 and L2 kernels; scaling to highly complex fused operators on advanced NPU clusters is left as future work. The 49.4% baseline-accuracy figure is stated without specifying which baseline framework produced it in the visible evidence. Speedup is reported as 'up to 2.2x' (best case); distribution across operator types is not fully exposed. Generalization beyond Ascend (Da Vinci/CANN) is claimed for Ascend 310/950 but not separately measured in the visible evidence.
facts.project_relevance: Hawk is a software/compiler-tooling contribution (NPU kernel generation via LLM + hardware-aware knowledge) rather than a new chip architecture; it is relevant to HW/SW codesign and the memory-IO codesign direction because it targets the Ascend memory hierarchy (Unified Buffer, L0/L1, MTE engines) and exposes how implicit hardware constraints dominate kernel performance. For the project card it addresses the software side of converting NPU peak compute into real throughput, not a silicon or packaging change.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.01590v2 (2 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from Sun Yat-sen University, GBA National Tech Innovation Center, Peng Cheng Laboratory.
Targets Ascend NPU (Da Vinci architecture, CANN toolchain); hardware platforms RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2.
The 49.4% baseline and 80.0% Hawk accuracy are consistently reported; the specific SOTA baseline behind 49.4% is not named in the visible evidence.
